title: The Clockwork Bakery
objective: Bake and serve three separate cooled bread batches on the bakery display without overproofing or burning any batch.
opening_narrative: You are the baker on the morning shift. Three empty batch bowls are waiting somewhere in the bakery, and the storeroom holds measured bread supplies. One mixer and two ovens must be shared. A real clock will run during your shift: while one dough rises, another batch can be mixed, proofed or baked. Read the recipe board, explore the cupboards, and keep an eye on every batch's readiness and deadline.

mixer.description: One batch at a time. Plug in and switch on, mix for 10 minutes, then start the rise to release the mixer. Its bowl remains accessible.

oven-a.name: Oven A
oven-a.description: An electric oven for one batch. Plug in and switch on before loading proofed dough. Bake for 30 minutes; unload within 10 more minutes or the bread burns.

oven-b.name: Oven B
oven-b.description: A second electric oven for an overlapping batch. The loaf remains accessible, but the oven is busy until unloading.

recipe-board.name: Bread recipe board
recipe-board.description: A readable recipe and shift timing guide fixed above the bench.
recipe-board.readable_text: For each of the three bowls measure one portion each of flour, water, yeast and salt in the storeroom. Carry measured bowls back to the bakery. Use a free powered mixer for 10 minutes. Start a 2-hour rise on the bench, which frees the mixer. Shape risen dough within 30 minutes; shaping starts a 45-minute proof. Load proofed dough into a free powered oven within 20 minutes. Bake 30 minutes and unload within 10 minutes after readiness to avoid burning. Cool on the rack for 20 minutes, then serve on the display. Read the observed clock mode: decision_paused freezes time during decisions and charges fixed simulated time for successful actions; continuous mode also runs during decisions. Interleave batches and prioritize imminent deadlines. Wait only when no useful task can be done. Appliance power must remain on while a batch occupies it. At 120x a 2-hour rise takes 60 real clock-running seconds. Pause freezes the clock.
